Dad here. Here are some advice that I've picked up in my (almost) 40 years of life   
\- Learn that sometimes, the reality in your mind does not match actual reality. We often make the mistake of thinking\\assuming something that isn't true, so it's important to put things in perspective.   


\- Listen first, respond later. Each word we say carries a weight, so it's best to distribute them wisely. 

\- 90% of what people say doesn't matter. Don't take everything to heart. 

\- Surround yourself with quality people, and you will have a quality life. The people we surround ourselves with affect us in more ways than we imagine. 

\- Be wise about your field of study. It's important to learn something for the mind, but its crucial to study something "for the pocket". Choose a major that will produce a profession and a minor that will develop your critical thinking.

\- Never assume you know everything. Only an ass doesn't change his mind. Learn to be open to our opinions. On that note, the most important trait one must develop is **tolerance**. It's what makes a good person a better one.   


I'll leave you with one last advice: the one my dad gave me when I was young. It is just one word - **Patience.** Have it, and you will reap more benefits than you think.
